plain_english: Arjuna asks Krsna about the steadfastness of those who, endowed with faith, act beyond scriptural rule, and whether their nature is sattva, rajas, or tamas; the Lord's answer follows according to faith.
sanskrit_cite: atha saptadaśo'dhyāyaḥ   arjuna uvāca   ye śāstravidhimutsṛtya vartante śraddhāyānvitāḥ | teṣāṃ  niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇā sattvamāho rajastamaḥ | śāstravidhimanālambya ye vyavahāramācaranti teṣāṃ kā gatiriti  praśnaḥ | tadatrottaraṃ śraddhānusāreṇa dīyate śrībhagavatā-

plain_english: The Lord says faith is threefold by nature, then explains scripture as unbiased, firm reflection rooted in knowing-freedom, fruitful for sattva-possessors with controlled conduct.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   trividhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṃ sā svabhāvajā | sāttvikī  rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti tāḥ śṛṇu | tatra cāyamāśayaḥ śāstraṃ nāma kila  pakṣapātārūṣitabuddhipūrvakatvavihīnam tathā  parāmarśadārḍhyarūpaṃ bodhasvātantryādeva  dṛḍhaparāmṛṣṭatayā phalādisvabhāvam  śuddhavimarśaniḥṣyandavāktattvaparamārthaparabrahmasvabhāvam  svatantraprasaratayā āntarādbodhasvabhāvādbahiḥ prasaraparyantam  susūkṣmapraṇavādirūpāt  vyavahāraprasiddhapravādaparamparāparyantam | yadāha-   tadvidāṃ ca smṛtiśīle | iti | tacca svata eva hitāhitopadeśāya kāryākāryavivecakam | yasya  svabhāvata eva sattvātirekasukumāraṃ hṛdayaṃ tenācaritaṃ  śāstritameva | anyastu rajastamaḥ kaluṣīkṛtaḥ  śāstroktamapyācarannācarati-śāstrārthasya  kārtsnyenānanuṣṭhānāt | śāstraṃ hi sattvavatāmeva phalavaditi  śāstramevāha-   yasya hastau ca pādau ca manaścaiva susaṃyatam | vidyā tapaśca  śīlaṃ ca sa tīrthaphalamaśnute | iti nānyo'saṃyatatvāt | tasmācchāstrārthaḥ parityaktakāmakrodha  moheṣu saphala iti tātparyamasyādhyāyasya tadevaitatpratāyate  spaṣṭārthatvācca na vivriyate | kintu kevalaṃ  pāṭhavipratipattinivāraṇāyaiva likhyate

plain_english: Faith is according to one's sattva; a person is made of faith, and he becomes according to his faith.
sanskrit_cite: sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata | śraddhāmayo'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ

plain_english: Sattvic people worship gods, yakshas, and rakshasas; rajasic and tamasic people worship spirits, ghosts, and demons.
sanskrit_cite: yajante sāttvikā devānyakṣarakṣāṃsi rājasāḥ | bhūtapretapiśācāṃśca yajante tāmasā janāḥ

plain_english: People joined with hypocrisy and ego, endowed with desire, attachment, and force, perform terrible austerity not prescribed by scripture.
sanskrit_cite: aśāstravihitaṃ ghoraṃ tapastapyanti ye janāḥ | dambhāhaṅkārasaṃyuktāḥ kāmarāgabalānvitāḥ

plain_english: Those who torment the body and the Lord within are demonic; they are connected to faith turned elsewhere, fashion self-made austerity, and are tamasic.
sanskrit_cite: karṣayantaḥ śarīrasthaṃ bhūtagrāmamacetanam | māṃ  caivāntaḥśarīrasthaṃ tānviddhyāsuraniścayān | sattvānurūpā-ityatra sattvaśabdaḥ svabhāvaparyāyaḥ | ayaṃ  puruṣaḥ-ātmā śraddhayā anyavyāpāroparivartinyā avaśyaṃ  saṃbaddhaḥ | sa ca tanmaya eva boddhavyaḥ | acetanam-avivekitvāt | māṃ ca karṣayantaḥ-śāstrārthānanuṣṭhānāt | ata eva te  svabuddhiviracitāṃ tapaścaryāṃ kurvāṇāḥ pratyuta tāmasāḥ | āhāro'pi sattvādibhedāt tridhā śraddhāvat | tathā  yajñatapodānāni-taducyate-

plain_english: Food is threefold for all, and sacrifice, austerity, and gift are likewise threefold; hear this distinction.
sanskrit_cite: āhārastvapi sarvasya trividho bhavati priyaḥ | yajñastapastathā  dānaṃ teṣāṃ bhedamimaṃ śṛṇu

plain_english: Foods that increase life, purity, strength, health, joy, and affection, being tasty, unctuous, steady, and heart-pleasing, are dear to sattva.
sanskrit_cite: āyuḥsattvabalārogyasukhaprītivivardhanāḥ | rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ  sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvikapriyāḥ

plain_english: Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, very hot, sharp, dry, and burning are desired by rajas and give pain, grief, and disease.
sanskrit_cite: kaṭvamlalavaṇātyuṣṇatīkṣṇarūkṣavidāhinaḥ | āhārā  rājasasyeṣṭā duḥkhaśokāmayapradāḥ

plain_english: Food that is stale, tasteless, putrid, leftover, and impure is dear to tamas.
sanskrit_cite: yātayāmaṃ gatarasaṃ pūti paryuṣitaṃ ca yat | ucchiṣṭamapi  cāmedhyaṃ bhojanaṃ tāmasapriyam | yātayāmamiti-yātā yāmā yasya

plain_english: A sacrifice performed by those not desiring fruit, according to rule, with the mind fixed on duty alone, is sattvic.
sanskrit_cite: aphalākāṃkṣibhiryajño vidhidṛṣṭo ya ijyate | yaṣṭavyamityeva  manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ | manaḥ samādhāya-niścayenānusandhāya

plain_english: Know that a sacrifice performed aiming at fruit and for show is rajasic, unsteady, and impermanent.
sanskrit_cite: abhisandhāya tu phalaṃ dambhārthamapi caiva yataḥ | ijyate viddhi  taṃ yajñaṃ rājasaṃ calamadhruvam | dambhārthamapīti | dambho-loko māmevaṃvidhaṃ jānīyāditi

plain_english: They declare tamasic a sacrifice that lacks rule, has unoffered food, lacks mantra, is giftless, and is devoid of faith. 'Lacking rule' means lacking scripture-prescribed action, and that same sacrifice is elaborated by qualifiers such as unoffered food.
sanskrit_cite: vidhihīnamasṛṣṭānnaṃ mantrahīnamadakṣiṇam | śraddhāvirahitaṃ  yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate | vidhihīnamiti-śāstrīktakriyāhīnam | tadevāsṛṣṭānnādibhirviśeṣaṇairvitanyate

plain_english: Worship of gods, twice-born, teachers, and the wise; purity and straightforwardness; celibacy and non-injury—this is called bodily austerity. Straightforwardness or rectitude, not concealing objects, and boldness are also mentioned.
sanskrit_cite: devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṃ śaucamārjavam | brahmacaryamahiṃsā ca  śārīraṃ tapa ucyate | ārjavam-ṛjutā | (agopyaviṣayā dhṛṣṭatā)

plain_english: Speech that does not distress, is true, pleasant, and beneficial is called speech-born austerity, along with self-study and practice. "Truth" means determining this very essential nature; "pleasant and beneficial" means pleasant at that time and beneficial at another time. Such speech is called truth, not merely recounting events.
sanskrit_cite: anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priyahitaṃ ca yat | svādhyāyābhyasanaṃ caiva vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate | satyamiti | asyaiva svarūpanirūpaṇaṃ priyahitam-ityanena kriyate | priyaṃ ca tatkāle hitaṃ ca kālāntare | īdṛśaṃ vākyaṃ  satyamityucyate natu yathāvṛttakathanamātram

plain_english: Mental austerity is said to be mental serenity, gentleness, silence, self-control, and purity of being; purity of being is the complete purification of one's intention or inner disposition.
sanskrit_cite: manaḥprasādaḥ saumyatvaṃ maunamātmavinigrahaḥ | bhāvasaṃśuddhirityetattapo mānasamucyate | bhāvaḥ-āśayaḥ tasya samyak śuddhiḥ bhāvasaṃśuddhiḥ

plain_english: Men declare as sattvic the threefold austerity that is endowed with supreme faith and performed by those who are free from desire for fruit.
sanskrit_cite: śraddhayā parayopetaṃ tapastattrividham naraiḥ | aphalākāṃkṣibhiryuktaiḥ sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate

plain_english: Austerity performed with hypocrisy for the sake of honor, respect, or worship is here declared rajasic, unstable, and impermanent.
sanskrit_cite: satkāramānapūjārthaṃ tapo dambhena caiva yat | kriyate tadiha  proktaṃ rājasaṃ calamadhruvam

plain_english: Austerity performed with foolish self-torment or to destroy another is tamasic; in all three kinds, faith is sattvic, rajasic, or tamasic according to its aim.
sanskrit_cite: mūḍhagrāheṇātmano yatpīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ | parasyotsādanārthaṃ vā tattāmasamudāhṛtam | trividhe'pi tapasi śraddhā | sāttvikasya hi tanmayī eva śraddhā | rājasasya tu rajasi-dambhādāveva śraddhā | tamoniṣṭhasya punaḥ  parotsādanādāveva śraddhā | iti trividhamapi tapaḥ sraddhayopetaṃ  munirāha

plain_english: A gift given to an unhelpful person at the right place and time to a worthy recipient is sattvic; mere obligation is only to be observed.
sanskrit_cite: dātavyamiti yaddānaṃ dīyate'nupakāriṇe | deśe kāle ca pātre ca  taddānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam | dātavyamiti-dadyātiti niyogamātraṃ pālanīyamiti

plain_english: A gift given for reciprocal benefit or with an eye to fruit, or given in distress, is called rajasic.
sanskrit_cite: yattu pratyupakārārthaṃ phalamuddiśya vā punaḥ | dīyate ca  parikliṣṭaṃ tadrājasamiti smṛtam | doṣābhisandhānāya parikliṣṭaṃ-mitādidoṣāt

plain_english: A gift given at the wrong place or time to unworthy recipients, disrespectfully, is tamasic; worldly actions are explained by threefold intent, and now the manner of those beyond the three strands is stated.
sanskrit_cite: adeśakāle yaddānamapātrebhyaśca dīyate | asatkṛtamavajñātaṃ  tattāmasamudāhṛtam | dānasya cāsatkaraṇaṃ tatsaṃpradānādyasatkaraṇāt | evaṃ  laukikānāṃ sāttvikāditriprakārāśayānusāreṇa kriyā  vyākhyātā | idānīṃ ye guṇatritayasaṃkaṭottīrṇadhiyaste kriyāṃ  kathamācarantīti tādṛk prakāra ucyate-

plain_english: Om tat sat is the threefold designation of brahman; by it brahmins, vedas, and sacrifices were prescribed formerly.
sanskrit_cite: oṃ tatsaditi nirdeśo brahmaṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ | brāhmaṇāstena  vedāśca yañāśca vihitāḥ purā

plain_english: Therefore, uttering om, the prescribed actions of sacrifice, gift, and austerity proceed always among speakers of brahman.
sanskrit_cite: tasmādomityudāhṛtya yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥ | pravartante  vidhānoktāḥ satataṃ brahmavādinām

plain_english: Liberation-seekers perform various sacrifice, austerity, and gift actions without desiring their fruit.
sanskrit_cite: tadityanabhisandhāya phalaṃ yajñatapaḥkriyāḥ | dānakriyāśca  vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣakāṅkṣibhiḥ

plain_english: The word sat is used in existence and goodness, and likewise in praiseworthy action; so, O Partha, sat is sung.
sanskrit_cite: sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca sadityetatprayujyate | praśaste karmaṇi  tathā sacchabdaḥ pārtha gīyate

plain_english: Steadiness in sacrifice, austerity, and gift is called sat, and action done for that purpose is also called sat. Om, tat, and sat are three words that designate and manifest Brahman: om indicates scriptural meaning tied to embodiment, tat denotes generality and non-attachment to fruits, and sat declares praise. Action performed with a corrupt intellect becomes tamasic, while action done without attachment to specific fruits is not binding. Thus faithful sacrifice, austerity, and gift do not bind, whereas faithless action is tamasic and fruitless.
sanskrit_cite: yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ saditi cocyate | karma caiva  tadarthīyaṃ sadityevābhidhīyate | oṃ-tat-sat-ityebhistribhiḥ śabdairbrahmaṇo  nirdeśaḥ-saṃmukhīkaraṇam | tatra om-ityanena  śāstrārtho'yamādehasaṃbandhamūrīkārya iti sūcyate | tat-iti  sarvanāmapadena sāmānyamātrābhidhāyinā  viśeṣaparāmarśamātrāsamarthena phalānabhisaṃdhānaṃ  brahmaṇyucyate abhisaṃdhānasya viśeṣaparigrahamantareṇābhāvāt  sakalaviśeṣānugrāhisve'pi sakalaphalasaṃdhāne  sarvakartṛtāyāmapi viśiṣṭaphalāyogāt | sat-ityamuyā śrutyā  praśaṃsābhidhīyate | kriyamāṇamapīdaṃ yajñādikaṃ duṣṭamiti  buddhyā kriyamāṇaṃ tāmasatāmeti | viśiṣṭaphalābhidhānena ca  kriyamāṇaṃ na ca sat bandhādhāyakameveti | tasmāt  kartavyamidam-iti manvānā yajñādi kurvāṇā api na badhyante | anenaivābhiprāyeṇādiparvaṇyuktaṃ-   tapo na kalko'dhyayanaṃ na kalkaḥ svābhāviko vedavidhirna kalkaḥ | prasahya vittāharaṇaṃ na kalkastānyeva bhāvopahatāni kalkaḥ | (mahā0 bhā0)   iti | kalkaḥ-bandhakaḥ | svābhāvika iti brāhmaṇena niṣkāraṇaṃ  ṣaḍaṅgaṃ vedādi adhyetavyam-iti | prasahya-śāstralokaprasiddhocitayā ceṣṭayā | bhāvena-sattvādiguṇatrayayoginā cittena upahatānyetānyeva  bandhakāni nānyatheti tātparyam | ato yajñādi  yāvaccharīrabhāvitayā kāryameva | tadarthe vihitaṃ karma-arjanādi | yadi vā-om-ityanena samupaśāntasamastaprapañcam | tat-ityanenodbhidyamānaviśvataraṅgaparāmarśamātrātmakecchāsvāta  ntryasva-bhāvam | sat-ityanenecchāsvātantryabharavijṛmbhamāṇabhedakam pūrṇatve'pi  tāvaccitrasvabhāvatayā bhavanamiti pratipādyate | tathā coktaṃ  sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca iti | tena paramaṃ praśāntaṃ rūpaṃ  puraskṛtya ditsā-yiyakṣātitapsātmakecchātaraṅgasaṃgataṃ ca  madhyekṛtya dānayajñatapaḥkriyākarakakalāpaparipūrṇaṃ  yaccaramaṃ vapuridamullasitam etatkhalu samaṃ tritayamanargalasya  svābhāvikaṃ rūpam iti kasya kiṃ kathaṃ kutaḥ kva kena phalaṃ  syāditi | idānīmaśraddhāvataḥ tāmasaṃ karma sarvathaiva  niṣphalam-kārakakalāpasaṃyojanasamupajanitaprayāsamātraphalameva  iti sarvathā aśraddhāvatā na bhāvyamityucyate-

plain_english: Whatever is offered, given, or done as austerity without faith is called asat; it avails neither here nor hereafter. Therefore those who strive in auspicious action attain śivam with ease.
sanskrit_cite: aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattaṃ tapastaptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat | asadityucyate  pārtha na ca tatpretya no iha | asaditi-apraśastam | tasmātpraśaste karmaṇi yatamānānāṃ  sukhenaiva bhavati śivamiti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: that is indeed agent-entry; action is non-distinct from it; nevertheless, for knowers, it culminates in liberation.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   sa eva kārakāveśaḥ kriyā saivāviśeṣiṇī | tathāpi  vijñānavatāṃ mokṣārthe paryavasyati | iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe saptadaśo'dhyāyaḥ
